Class GameController

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsw.am56.controller.GameController
public class GameController extends Object
Server-side entry point that turns client actions into operations on the GameModel. It is the receiver of the command pattern: each ClientRequest ultimately calls one of the methods below, which validate the request, mutate the model and let the model notify its observers.

All model access is guarded by synchronizing on the model instance (and the public mutators are themselves synchronized), so concurrent requests coming from different connections are serialized. The controller also owns the reconnection window used to decide, after a disconnection, whether the game can resume or must be aborted.

  • Method Details

    • startReconnectWindow

      public void startReconnectWindow(Set<String> expected, long timeoutMs)
      Opens a reconnection window after a disconnection: it records which players are expected to reconnect and schedules a deadline. If, when the timeout elapses, not all expected players have reconnected, the game is aborted via handleDisconnect().
      Parameters:
      expected - the nicknames that must reconnect for the game to resume
      timeoutMs - how long (in milliseconds) to wait for all reconnections

    • handleDisconnect

      public void handleDisconnect()
      Aborts the current game following an unrecovered disconnection: it notifies the model (so the remaining clients are told the game was aborted), deletes the saved game so it cannot be resumed, and then shuts the server process down shortly afterwards.

    • acceptsNewConnections

      public boolean acceptsNewConnections()
      Tells whether the server may register a brand-new client connection right now. Connections are accepted while the lobby is still filling (so players can join) and while a reconnection window is open (so previously-connected players can come back after a server restart), but are refused once the game is in progress. This stops outsiders from connecting mid-game, which otherwise let them resume under an existing player's nickname, or abort the whole game for everyone else just by closing their terminal even though they were never actually playing.
      Returns:
      true if a new connection may be registered, false if it must be refused

    • reconnectPlayer

      public void reconnectPlayer(String nickname) throws InvalidActionException
      Reconnects a player to a game in progress. The nickname must match one already in the game; on success the player is re-synced with the current game state and, if a reconnection window is open, counted among those who have come back (closing the window once everyone has reconnected).
      Parameters:
      nickname - the nickname of the reconnecting player
      Throws:
      InvalidActionException - if no player with that nickname exists in the current game

    • moveTotem

      public void moveTotem(String nickname, String offerTileLetter) throws InvalidActionException

      Throws:
